modern_technique_gaps.gap: The Python sidecar's per-request `dropped_frames` counter is stranded at the IPC boundary: `PluginEvent::Done { request_id }` (crates/voicekit-ipc/src/message.rs:160/162) carries no drop field, so serde tolerates-and-discards it and `TurnDone.dropped_frames` reflects only the Rust playout `AudioRing`. The bounded buffer's loss telemetry never reaches the runtime/CLI, so the new bound is inert end-to-end (the Rust client also sends the utterance as a single frame).
modern_technique_gaps.suggested_remedy: Add `dropped_frames: Option<u64>` (or `#[serde(default)]`) to `PluginEvent::Done`, have the Python terminal done populate it, and aggregate it into `TurnReport`/`SessionEvent::TurnDone` so sidecar-side loss is observable. Keep the accept-and-count or reject policy explicit.

modern_technique_gaps.gap: No property-based coverage of the new `EventQueue` invariants. The plan's tier-3 deliverable asked for capacity monotonicity / counted drops / control-event preservation property tests, but the tier-3 verifier passed vacuously (`"vacuous": true`, no fast-check/no stryker) and the new tests are example-based only. `crates/voicekit-runtime` has no `proptest` dev-dependency and no `tests/properties.rs`, though `crates/voicekit-core/tests/properties.rs` already models the pattern for `AudioRing`.
modern_technique_gaps.suggested_remedy: Add `proptest.workspace = true` to voicekit-runtime [dev-dependencies] and a tests/properties.rs asserting `accepted + dropped == pushes`, `depth <= capacity`, no control event ever missing from `take()`, and the reserved terminal slot invariant, mirroring crates/voicekit-core/tests/properties.rs.

modern_technique_gaps.gap: No producer-side / adaptive backpressure. The event and audio queues are lossy-only (`DropOldest`/`DropNewest`) with no Block/credit signal to the producer, so the drop counter is reported but never consumed; modern stream-processing practice pairs shedding with admission control.
modern_technique_gaps.suggested_remedy: Add a Block/credit policy (or per-lane policy) or consume the drop counter to throttle the producer; document lossy-by-design for the realtime path if a throttle is out of scope.

modern_technique_gaps.gap: The Python plugin's `cancelled` tombstone set is the one unbounded structure in the change (plugin.py:112): a cancelled id is inserted at :206-207 and removed only on id reuse (:185) or a late audio_end (:272), so a host that cancels and never sends audio_end leaves a permanent entry. Also, once the tombstone is discarded on the first late audio_end, post-cancel audio can be re-buffered and a second late audio_end yields a protocol error (unreachable via the shipped Rust client, which sends one AudioEnd per request).
modern_technique_gaps.suggested_remedy: Keep cancelled ids tombstoned (do not discard on late audio_end) or bound/age the set (bounded deque/LRU/TTL) and treat any later audio_end for a tombstoned id as a silent no-op; add a pytest for two late audio_end frames and post-cancel audio leaving pending_audio empty.

modern_technique_gaps.gap: The CLI parity test is a framing round-trip, not a differential test against the real Python plugin: both sides are built from the same in-process fakes (FAKE_LLM_DELTAS/FakeTts), so a divergence in the Python plugin would not fail it; the real plugin is exercised only by the printing demo (P4).
modern_technique_gaps.suggested_remedy: Add a Python-gated/`#[ignore]`d integration test (or snapshot the Python protocol transcript) that asserts the real plugin's scripted turn produces the same event trace as the fake path. The current in-process double is plan-sanctioned and may remain as the hermetic CI gate.

modern_technique_gaps.gap: v0 turn model is half-duplex (strictly sequential VAD->STT->LLM->TTS); early-start/pipelined decoding is not implemented. This is the main latency gap versus 2025-2026 frontier practice and is explicitly declared a non-goal in docs/adr/0001-architecture.md:66-73 rather than silently shipped.
modern_technique_gaps.suggested_remedy: Track as a v0.1 item (early-start/pipelined decoding, jitter-aware/adaptive buffering). No action this iteration: the ADR honestly documents it as a non-goal and does not claim it is implemented.

low_confidence_claims.claim: RESOLVED (3-lens consensus, false as an end-to-end claim): 'The sidecar's per-request dropped_frames counter is observable in TurnDone.' codex, kimi, and minimax all verified serde tolerates the extra Python field but that `PluginEvent::Done` has no field to carry it, so the count dies at the IPC boundary; `TurnDone.dropped_frames` is Rust-ring-only and both are 0 in P4, so the run cannot distinguish no-drops from not-plumbed.

RESOLVED (3-lens consensus): 'The unbounded Python `cancelled` tombstone set is a hard-rule violation.' kimi, glm, and minimax each examined it and concluded it is a request-lifecycle ledger of ids (not a payload-accumulating audio/event queue) and is unreachable as a growth path from the shipped client; minimax's confidence reading it as non-violation is ~75%, but all three classify it as residual risk, not a violation.

RESOLVED (3-lens consensus): 'The tier-1/2/3 verifier artifacts provide independent machine-verified coverage for this Rust+Python repo.' codex, kimi, and minimax all show the artifacts are JS/TS-shaped and vacuous (tier3 `"vacuous": true`); the panel therefore substituted its own serial P1-P6 reruns, which agree with the implementer logs.

RESOLVED (3-lens consensus): 'The plan's tier-3 property coverage for the new EventQueue was delivered.' codex, glm, and minimax all find only example-based tests and a vacuous tier-3 verifier; recorded as the non-blocking modern-technique gap above.

RESOLVED (3-lens consensus): 'The parity test demonstrates behavioural parity with the real Python plugin.' codex, kimi, and minimax all find it compares fake-vs-fake through voicekit-ipc framing, so it proves framing parity only; the plan explicitly permits an in-process double, so this is conformant, not a probe failure.

SINGLE-LENS (operator review): P4's sidecar child was reaped cleanly; the demo log has no explicit shutdown-ack line and the claim is inferred from exit 0 plus the awaited client.shutdown() path. ~85% confident.

SINGLE-LENS (operator review): `rustfmt --check` passed on all touched Rust files; recorded only as a textual note in implementer-summary.json with no captured command output. ~75% confident (formatting is not a DoD probe).

SINGLE-LENS (operator review): control-lane overflow leaves the session state machine in Thinking without emitting Failed or returning to Listening, so a subsequent run_turn could hit an illegal transition; derived by reading session.rs:284-292 + turn.rs:99-135, not reproduced, and only reachable with a mis-set event_capacity or a non-draining transport.

SINGLE-LENS (operator review): ReplyDelta and AudioOut share one DropOldest policy, so a backpressured reply loses its prefix in the CLI trace while TurnReport.reply keeps the full text, letting trace and summary disagree after a drop.

SINGLE-LENS: audio arriving before its request message is discarded and uncounted (plugin.py:183-184), and an out-of-order cancel can be silently un-done on later request-start (:185); both unreachable through the shipped client's write order. Control lane also has no separate reserved ring, so TranscriptFinal can be refused under sustained backpressure even though it was never evictable — this is the plan-prescribed loud-failure behaviour.

reasons: DoD: 6/6 probes pass with unanimous 4/4 lens agreement on rerun (P1 69 tests/0 fail exit 0; P2 fake demo exit 0 with only in-process fakes; P3 22 pytest passed; P4 sidecar demo exit 0 with TurnDone dropped_frames/dropped_ms/dropped_events and a reaped child; P5 compound rg exit 0, negated rg found no old field form; P6 full chained success command exit 0).

Hard rules: no lens reported any violation. Every lens independently confirmed bounded queue + explicit policy + counter on both sides (events.rs:98-190, session.rs:38-40, plugin.py:32-36,87-105,310-319), control events never silently dropped and loud Protocol failure on control overflow, a reserved terminal TurnDone slot, no Python in the default turn, an untouched TurnState table (voicekit-core undiffed; illegal_transition test still passes), a single MonoClock with no wall-clock in the diff, idempotent non-fatal purge-then-ack cancel, no network/API keys, and protected paths clean (kickoffs/voicekit-rsi-hardening.md is pre-existing per pre-implementer-untracked, not child-owned).

Scope provenance: implementer-summary.json touched_files[] exactly matches git status (11 paths: Cargo.lock, crates/voicekit-cli/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs,src/main.rs,tests/parity.rs}, crates/voicekit-runtime/src/{events.rs,lib.rs,session.rs}, docs/adr/0001-architecture.md, sdks/python/tests/test_plugin.py, sdks/python/voicekit_sdk/plugin.py).

The prior escalation's two items are closed: the sidecar's per-request audio is now a bounded deque (MAX_PENDING_AUDIO_FRAMES=64, drop_oldest, monotonic per-request counter surfaced as dropped_frames) and cancel is honest purge-then-ack, idempotent, non-fatal, unknown-id no-op ack; the runtime's unbounded `events: Vec<SessionEvent>` is replaced by a counted EventQueue with a reserved terminal slot and loud control-lane failure.

Modern-technique gaps are all non-blocking: sidecar loss telemetry not plumbed past the IPC boundary (codex/kimi/minimax), no proptest coverage of EventQueue (codex/glm/minimax), no adaptive backpressure (codex/kimi/glm), the unbounded cancelled tombstone set (all four, classified non-violation), a framing-only parity test (codex/kimi/minimax), and the documented half-duplex v0 boundary. None fails a DoD probe and none is a hard-rule violation, and all four lenses independently returned APPROVE; they are recorded as follow-ups, not blockers.

Low-confidence claims resolved by consensus: all multi-lens flagged claims (sidecar counter not end-to-end, tombstone not a violation, tier artifacts vacuous, tier-3 property unimplemented, parity is framing-only) are consistent across 3+ lenses and are treated as resolved using Verify-when-Uncertain (2502.15845 Alg 1). The remaining single-lens uncertainties (child-reap visibility, rustfmt note, control-overflow state-machine edge, shared-lane DropOldest prefix loss, out-of-order/uncounted pre-request audio) are surfaced below the approval bar for operator review.

Disagreement on evidence provenance noted but not load-bearing: glm accepted the recorded tier/implementer evidence, while codex/kimi/minimax found the tier artifacts vacuous and reran every probe; both paths converge on the same 6/6 pass result, so the probe outcomes are not disputed.
